title: Lessons of Past Nations and the Purpose of Creation

paragraphs.text: More signs are found in the stories of earlier nations. When Allah sent a barren, destructive wind against 'Aad, it turned everything it touched into crumbling ruins. The people of Thamud were told to enjoy themselves for a limited time, but they insolently rebelled against their Lord's command. So a thunderbolt seized them while they were watching, and they could neither stand up nor defend themselves. Before all of them, the people of Noah were also destroyed, because they were a people who stubbornly disobeyed.

Allah built the heaven with great strength, and He is continually expanding it. He spread out the earth, and He prepares it in an excellent way for His creatures. He created everything in pairs, so that people might remember and reflect. Therefore, the Prophet calls people to flee to Allah, and he declares that he is a clear warner sent from Him. He also warns them not to set up any other deity alongside Allah, repeating that he is a clear warner from Him.

This kind of rejection is nothing new. Every messenger who came to earlier peoples was called either a magician or a madman. It is as if they had passed this insult down to one another, though in fact they were simply a people who exceeded all limits. The Prophet is told to turn away from them, since he will not be blamed for their choices. Yet he should keep reminding, because reminding brings real benefit to the believers.

Then comes a central statement about the purpose of existence. Allah says that He created the jinn and mankind only so that they would worship Him. He does not need any provision from them, nor does He ask them to feed Him, since He is completely free of need. It is Allah alone who is the constant Provider of all creation, the Owner of firm and unshakable strength. Every living thing depends on Him, while He depends on nothing at all.
